ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-engagement and ongoing screening of all general partners, all limited partners holding 25% or greater economic interest, all authorized signatories, and all agents against the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list, the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, and Canada's Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List under the Special Economic Measures Act; mandatory politically exposed person (PEP) determination at domestic and foreign levels for principals, with enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth verification, and senior management approval required for any PEP determination; transaction monitoring applied to all payout rails including Google AdMob and AppLovin payouts with automatic red-flag escalation to FINTRAC reporting where applicable.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: British Columbia Corporate Registry - OneStop Business Registry (corporateonline.gov.bc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory names filed in BC must be presented in English; a French version may be registered only alongside the English form; numerals may be expressed as figures or words; names must not include punctuation marks or symbols other than standard separators; non-Latin script names are accepted only in romanized transliteration with a certified declaration of meaning; all proposed names require a NUANS pre-screening report to establish distinctiveness under the Business Corporations Act and the Partnership Act name-approval criteria.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The BC name approval is valid for 56 days and may be extended for one further 56-day period upon written request to the Registrar of Companies prior to expiry. Where a name is rejected, the applicant may resubmit a revised name through the OneStop portal at no additional fee within 30 days, or file a formal administrative reconsideration request with the Registrar of Companies providing evidence of distinctiveness, acquired goodwill, and compliance with the BC Name Requirements; a negative reconsideration decision may be challenged by judicial review in the Supreme Court of British Columbia under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, RSBC 1996, c 241.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual registered-office arrangement is accepted by the BC Registry provided that a licensed BC registered agent maintains a physical service address in British Columbia at which statutory records and the partnership register are physically available; a purely non-physical virtual address without a records location does not satisfy the Partnership Act records-keeping mandate. For the hyper-casual gaming industry no operating staff or physical studio is required, and outsourced development, hosting, and ad-monetization operations are fully compatible with the LP structure provided the general partner is duly constituted and registered.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low, estimated at under 5% annually for newly registered LPs without a regulatory license trigger; the BC Registrar does not conduct routine unannounced on-site inspections of limited partnership registered offices, but retains statutory authority to order production of records, and FINTRAC and the Canada Revenue Agency conduct desk-based compliance reviews with document production timelines typically set at 30 days or less.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Limited Partnership Act, RSBC 1996, c. 216, Part 2 (Creation and Registration of Limited Partnerships), ss. 6–13; Partnership Act, RSBC 1996, c. 348, ss. 2–4
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registry Services, Ministry of Citizens' Services (BC Registries and Online Services)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 – Declaration of Limited Partnership (filed under s. 8 of the Limited Partnership Act)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement; partner contributions are determined in the limited partnership agreement. No escrow account is mandated by BC law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the initial Limited Partnership Agreement of the Partnership be, and is hereby, adopted as the governing agreement effective as of the date of this Resolution. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Partnership shall be established at the address designated in the Declaration of Limited Partnership. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the General Partner appoints the individual named in the Declaration as the authorized representative for service of process in British Columbia. FURTHER RESOLVED, that all necessary filings, including the Declaration of Limited Partnership, be executed and submitted to BC Registry Services, and the General Partner’s secretary is directed to pay all required fees and correct any deficiencies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registry Services – OneStop Business Registry (online)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search and submit a name reservation request through the BC Registry online portal. The proposed name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing corporate, partnership, or trademark. Upon approval, the reservation is valid for 56 days.
required_dossiers: Signed authorization from all initial partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, submit an alternative name or file a written appeal with the Registrar within 30 days providing justification of distinctiveness.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Declaration of Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and execute Form 1 – Declaration of Limited Partnership, setting out the partnership name, registered office address, general partners, limited partners, and amount of contribution. Submit to BC Registry Services with the prescribed filing fee and proof of name reservation.
required_dossiers: Form 1 – Declaration of Limited Partnership signed by all general partners and initial limited partners
Notice of registered office (Form 2, if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar queries or rejects the declaration, correct the identified deficiencies and resubmit within 21 days. Where the registrar refuses registration, file an appeal under s. 11 of the Limited Partnership Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Partner and all limited partners (private action)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon issuance of the Certificate of Limited Partnership, the parties must execute a written limited partnership agreement, which shall address profit sharing, management controls, capital contributions, withdrawal and assignment rights, and dispute resolution. The agreement should be dated retroactively to the submission date but physically signed after registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any disagreement on terms is resolved through negotiation; if the partnership agreement is not executed, the statutory default provisions of the Limited Partnership Act govern the partnership.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of Business Number and Tax Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and BC Ministry of Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the partnership through the Business Registration Online (BRO) portal to obtain a Canada Revenue Agency Business Number (BN). Simultaneously register for GST/HST (if applicable), BC PST collection, and WorkSafeBC coverage. For partnerships, the BN is held by the partnership as a whole.
required_dossiers: General partner's personal identification and social insurance number
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA or provincial registration is delayed, contact the dedicated business line at 1-800-959-5525; amendments to registration can be processed through the same BRO portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business License and Physical Workspace Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipality (e.g., City of Vancouver Business License Office) and WorkSafeBC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a municipal business license for the registered office or any physical operating location. A fire and building occupancy inspection may be required. For a home-based virtual office, only a basic license is needed; for commercial premises, submit the certificate of limited partnership, lease agreement, and zoning compliance certificate. WorkSafeBC registration is required if hiring employees.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or proof of office address
Fire safety inspection report (for commercial premises only)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the license application is denied, appeal to the municipal licensing board or work with the local business liaison officer to rectify zoning or safety non-compliance. Interim remedial action includes operating exclusively online without a physical premises.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: BC Ministry of Jobs, Economic Development and Innovation (for digital publishing no specific industrial or manufacturing license is required)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Business License (if a physical office is maintained in BC)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: BC Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – software publishing and ad-funded mobile game development have no significant environmental footprint; no EIA or registration required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: None applicable – no industrial wastewater, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste generation. Standard office e-waste recycling and municipal solid waste disposal rules must be observed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: If a physical office is leased, obtain a fire safety inspection certificate from the local fire marshal, a building occupancy permit, and a workplace safety clearance under WorkSafeBC. A home-based office or fully virtual operation requires no civil defense clearance beyond the municipal business license.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — My Business Account portal at https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services.html; provincial Sales and Use taxes for British Columbia are administered by the BC Ministry of Finance, Consumer Taxation Branch at https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/taxes/consumption-taxes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must first obtain a 9-digit federal Business Number (BN) from the CRA, normally by using the 'Register a GST/HST Account' application in My Business Account or by filing Form RC1 'Request for a Business Number (BN)'. The BN is used across federal program accounts; a GST/HST account (RT) is created automatically when the person is engaged in commercial activity in Canada and exceeds the small-supplier threshold. For a BC limited partnership, the partnership itself, not the partners, is registered and files GST/HST returns. If the partnership makes taxable retail sales of goods or prescribed services in BC, it must separately register for the BC PST under the Consumer Taxation Branch. No separate annual 'TIN' number exists in Canada; the BN with its account suffix functions as the statutory TIN for federal tax filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a U.S.-style check-the-box regime. A BC limited partnership is per se fiscally transparent under section 96 of the Canadian Income Tax Act (ITA); every partner reports its partnership share directly. There is no election to treat the LP as a corporation for Canadian tax purposes, and CRA does not allow hybrid mismatch entity-classification elections. Optional elections that are available include (i) electing a non-calendar partnership fiscal period under ITA s. 249.1, and (ii) electing under ITA s. 97(2) to transfer property to a partnership on a rollover basis. For GST/HST, the LP is a 'person' registered in its own right under the Excise Tax Act; the partners do not have a check-the-box election for indirect tax.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) as administered by CRA; combined with British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST) at a separate 7% rate for prescribed taxable supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD $30,000: a person engaged in commercial activity in Canada must register for GST/HST when its worldwide taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in any single calendar quarter, or exceed CAD 30,000 in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters (small-supplier threshold). Non-resident digital vendors of specified digital products or remote services to Canadian consumers must register under the simplified GST/HST regime when their Canadian taxable revenues exceed CAD 30,000 in any 12-month period. A BC LP may also voluntarily register before the threshold is reached. No registration threshold applies to BC PST; a PST registration is required as soon as taxable goods or services are sold in BC unless a specific exemption applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not currently impose a mandatory real-time continuous transaction control (CTC) electronic-invoicing clearance regime, nor a fiscal stamping/API clearance obligation. CRA accepts both paper and electronic records; electronic invoices must be retained in a legible, readable format and be provided to CRA on demand. Registrants with annual GST/HST net tax remittances above CAD 1.5 million must file returns electronically (GST/HST NETFILE or EDI). There is no CRA API approval gate for invoice issuance; the CRA e-filing system is used for periodic tax returns, not individual invoice clearance. Withholding of GST/PST outside the ad platform is not required, but the transaction must be supported by invoices carrying the partnership's BN/GST registration reference.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: GST/HST zero-rating applies to the export of tangible personal property if the property is supplied to a non-resident, is not acquired for use in Canada, is exported as part of the supply, and all documentary evidence is obtained within specified time limits (ETA ss. 20-23). For services and intangible/digital property, a supply is zero-rated when made to a non-resident for use wholly outside Canada and is not in respect of real property or tangible personal property situated in Canada. For a hyper-casual game publisher organised as a BC LP, revenues generated by overseas ad-monetisation platforms (e.g., AdMob, AppLovin) and sales of digital game content to non-resident consumers may qualify for zero-rating if the contractual supply is received by a non-resident and the service/game is not used in Canada. However, any supply made in Canada (including ad mediation for Canadian users or in-app purchases made by Canadian consumers) is ordinarily subject to GST/HST at 5% on the supply value.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Form B13A / CBSA Export Declaration filed electronically through the Canadian Export Reporting System for goods exported by sea, air, or post if above prescribed thresholds
Commercial invoice and purchase/sales contract evidencing the supply to the non-resident purchaser
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill / proof of export (carrier evidence, freight documents or delivery confirmation in the case of digital services, geo-IP delivery logs)
Export packing list and shipping manifest (where physical goods are involved)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT/remittance advice evidencing receipt of export proceeds within the legislated FX repatriation window
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess a zero-rated export claim within the normal reassessment period of four years; where misrepresentation, neglect or fraud is alleged, the review period is unlimited. If the documentary evidence is inadequate, the CRA will disallow zero-rating, reverse the export refund and assess GST/HST, penalty and compound daily interest. Civil penalties for knowingly making a false or gross-negligent statement can reach 25% of the tax amount at issue. Criminal tax evasion under the Excise Tax Act and Income Tax Act carries fines of not less than 50% and not more than 200% of the tax sought to be evaded, plus imprisonment, and the CRA also has ancillary penalties for failure to provide documents. Retrospective clawbacks can include the denial of refunds for all prior quarters within the four-year window and the reassessment of the partnership's net tax.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as monetary authority; prudential bank supervision by OSFI; trade and cross-border financial intelligence by FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act. Canada maintains no standing foreign-exchange control statute; the Currency Act and the Bank of Canada Act govern. Cross-border currency and monetary instruments of CAD 10,000 or more must be reported at the border, and large-value electronic funds transfers (CAD 10,000+) to or from Canada are subject to FINTRAC reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: CAD is fully convertible under a free-floating regime for both current and capital account transactions. No exchange licensing, repatriation approval, or profit-remittance permits apply; partnership profits may be distributed to non-resident partners subject only to income tax withholding under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act and applicable tax treaty relief. The Investment Canada Act requires only a post-closing notification for a WTO foreign investor establishing a non-cultural Canadian business. Intra-group or third-party loan and capital inflows are unrestricted and may be denominated in any major currency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender timeline or mandatory conversion ratio applies to export or service proceeds. USD ad-network earnings (AdMob, AppLovin) may be held in USD accounts indefinitely without conversion. Treasury policy should, however, establish a periodic CAD remittance schedule from the USD concentration account to fund GST/PST obligations, payroll, and operating disbursements to avoid FX carry volatility.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) - integrating legacy HSBC Bank Canada network
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (CAD/USD dual-currency) and segregated USD Concentration Account
Operational Account with cross-border USD clearing via BMO Harris
Operational Account with eBusiness Liquidity Management

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High for payment facilitation, Low as a replacement for a Tier-1 concentration account. Wise, Payoneer, and Airwallex operate in Canada as registered Money Services Businesses under FINTRAC rather than chartered banks; they cannot take deposits under the Bank Act. A BC LP may use EMIs for vendor disbursements, contractor payouts, and working-capital floats, but must maintain the primary USD/CAD treasury at a Schedule I bank. EMI onboarding requires equivalent client identification verification (CIVR), and the LP must execute the EMI's separate MSB-compliant terms; outward EFTs above CAD 10,000 remain reportable to FINTRAC.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory mandate requires directors of the general partner to appear in person. Remote onboarding is permitted through dual-mode verification: (i) video-call KYC with document scanning, and (ii) an Affidavit of Identity executed before a notary, lawyer, accountant, or other authorized verifier under the PCMLTFA Regulations for any non-face-to-face signatory. In practice, most Tier-1 banks accept fully remote opening for Canadian-resident general partner directors; a non-Canadian-resident limited partner does not need to attend but must provide certified passport copies and source-of-wealth evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity of an LP: silent limited partners holding 99% interests without bank-visible identity, risking FINTRAC/Risk Assessment rejection.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: BC Registry transparent-ownership filing certificate, current Beneficial Ownership Schedule (name, DOB, residential address, nationality, exact percentage), full Limited Partnership Agreement, General Partner certificate of existence, and an organizational chart covering each partner to ultimate natural persons.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owners located in restricted or higher-risk jurisdictions, triggering enhanced due diligence (EDD).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passports, Global PEP/Sanctions clearance report from the bank's screening vendor, source-of-wealth package (bank statements, asset-management statements, two years of tax returns), and a written commercial rationale for the Canadian structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume small-value USD inflows from AdMob/AppLovin interpreted as splitting, funneling, or unexplained liquidity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Google AdSense/AdMob Publisher Agreement and AppLovin Publishing Agreement listing the LP as payee, rolling 12-month dashboard payout reports matched to ledger entries, sample MT103/SWIFT payment advices, and a board resolution confirming the monetization model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent partnership tax status causing CRA registration mismatches or failure to produce a Business Number, delaying account activation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CRA Business Number with RP0001 program account evidencing GST/HST registration, CRA 'Partnership Information Return Form T5013' filing acknowledgement, BC Partnership Registration certificate, and confirmation of the tax pass-through classification under the Income Tax Act.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid global payout velocity to contractors and ad agencies in 30+ jurisdictions, triggering sanctions/screen hits on intermediary banks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Approved payee registry with bank-verified KYC per payee, detailed payment-purpose save/notes fields referencing invoices and project codes, and an internal AML/CFT policy with an automated OFAC/EU/UN sanctions screen and hard-block logic.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: (i) the LP issues a written capital call stipulating each partner's contribution; (ii) remittance executes via SWIFT MT103 to the LP's USD or CAD concentration account, with Field 70 (Remittance Information) stating 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION - [Partner Name] - LP AGREEMENT [date]' and Field 72 referencing the capital call number; (iii) the bank obtains confirmation of the remitter for record; (iv) funds are posted to a capital-contribution subledger, never to the operating income account; (v) the bank retains the source-of-funds statement. FINTRAC large-EFT reporting applies above CAD 10,000; no Bank of Canada purpose-code declaration is required, but a contemporaneous Investment Canada Act assessment (usually notification-only for this sector) should be documented. Anti-money-laundering defense: retain capital call, contribution ledger, GL journal, and partner source-of-wealth on file.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rails: SWIFT MT103 for cross-border vendor/contractor payments; domestic non-urgent payouts via Payments Canada ACSS EFT (under 3-day settlement); urgent domestic CAD via the Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) real-time messaging; USD same-day via the bankÔÇôtoÔÇôbank US clearing network (Fedwire/CHIPS through the Canadian bank's USD correspondents). Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) are not standard for hyper-casual gaming service procurement; disbursements should be open-account with invoices and purchase orders. For FX conversion, execute a single daily USD-to-CAD trade at the concentration bank to minimize spreads, rather than per-invoice conversion. Dual-authority approval (treasury manager + CFO) applies to wire payments above CAD 50,000.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD FX forwards (bank-confirmable line at RBC/TD/BMO, 30-180 day tenors)
FX swaps (spot vs. forward and tomorrow-next rolls) for managing USD payout-date mismatches
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (USD/CAD) to fix long-term USD-denominated intercompany debt service
Vanilla FX options (CAD call/USD put purchased as an expense-based cap) to hedge adverse USD depreciation on contracted ad-network revenue
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on exotic currencies (e.g., USD/BRL, USD/CNH) where receivables arise from localized user acquisition agencies but remittance is ultimately in USD
Term deposits in USD/CAD to capture favorable yield while maintaining a laddered liquidity band equal to 4-6 months of operating burn

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Companies and Corporate Registries (BC Registries)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the anniversary of the partnership's registration date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD 50; continued non-filing for more than two years may trigger administrative strike-off or dissolution of the limited partnership.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return (where electing or required under the Income Tax Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after the partnership's fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly late-filing penalty equal to the product of the number of partners (up to $100 for each month) and 1% of the contributed capital; additional penalties for gross negligence or intentional omissions, plus administrative penalties under section 162 of the Income Tax Act.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None imposed by the British Columbia Limited Partnership Act or Canadian federal statute for a limited partnership per se. A mandatory independent audit is only triggered where the partnership agreement, a lender, an investor, or an order of the CRA requires audited financial statements. For hyper-casual gaming revenue streams, there is no industry-specific audit requirement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) — private partnerships commonly select ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises), or IFRS if required by the partnership agreement, cross-border investor, or for tax planning. The CRA does not impose a specific GAAP hierarchy but expects consistent application.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The BC Limited Partnership is not required to file a separate UBO register with BC Registries. Annual confirmation of all changes to general and limited partners is effectuated through the annual report and any intervening change filings. Federal beneficial-ownership transparency rules remain pending in Canada; a recommendation is to maintain an internal beneficial-ownership register and file amendments when requested by BC Registries or under mutual legal assistance.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of General Partners and Limited Partners
Record of Capital Contributions and Withdrawals
Minute book containing partnership resolutions and written consents (where prepared)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000–20,000 (only if contractually or commercially required)

stage_6.statutory_headline_rate: 27% combined (15% federal + 12% British Columbia provincial). The CA_LP is a fiscally transparent partnership; the combined rate is borne by corporate partners on their allocated share of Canadian-source active business income. Non-resident partners are subject to Part I tax at progressive rates (individual) or the 27% combined rate (corporate) on their share.
stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction for eligible CCPC partners: 11% combined (9% federal + 2% BC) on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income allocated through the LP, where the shareholder/partner conditions are met. SR&ED investment tax credits: 35% fully refundable ITC for qualifying CCPC partners on qualified expenditures up to CAD 3,000,000 (15% non-refundable/refundable for other corporate taxpayers). Additional BC innovation tax credits (e.g., BC Interactive Digital Media Tax Credit 17.5%) may apply to qualifying game development labour. Foreign tax credits available to partners for non-Canadian taxes paid.
